question: What is a vulval cyst?

options.A: An open sore caused by a bacterial infection
options.B: A fluid-filled sac on the external female genitalia
options.C: A solid overgrowth of muscle tissue in the pelvis
options.D: A cancerous tumor of the uterine lining

explanation: Vulval cysts are benign fluid-filled sacs located on or beneath the skin of the vulva. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T7#GNS216_U5_T7_h1)

question: Why do patients with newly discovered vulval cysts often feel very anxious?

options.A: Doctors usually misdiagnose it as a severe systemic infection
options.B: It automatically causes total infertility in young women
options.C: They frequently mistake the lump for a cancerous growth
options.D: The condition always requires immediate emergency surgery

explanation: Finding any unexplained lump can be scary! Patients often worry about cancer right away until a nurse or doctor calmly explains that it is benign. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T7#GNS216_U5_T7_h1)

question: What usually causes a Bartholin duct cyst to form?

options.A: Hormonal overproduction by the adrenal cortex
options.B: Blockage of the gland duct causing fluid to back up
options.C: Direct bacterial invasion from the urinary bladder
options.D: A genetic absence of the external genitalia glands

explanation: When the tiny tube (duct) leading from the Bartholin gland gets blocked, the fluid has nowhere to go and builds up into a cyst. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T7#GNS216_U5_T7_h2)

question: How do epidermal inclusion cysts typically form on the vulva?

options.A: Blocked sweat glands swell up during hot weather conditions
options.B: Surface skin cells get trapped beneath the skin after trauma or surgery
options.C: Embryonic remnants fill with fluid during puberty development
options.D: Infected hair follicles burst open and trap blood underneath

explanation: Sometimes, after an episiotomy, minor injury, or surgery, surface skin cells get pushed deeper under the tissue where they form a little fluid pocket. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T7#GNS216_U5_T7_h2)

question: What is usually the main symptom of a small, uninfected vulval cyst?

options.A: No symptoms at all; it is often found during routine exams
options.B: Severe, throbbing pain that shoots down the legs
options.C: High fever and uncontrollable shivering chills
options.D: Continuous bleeding from the vaginal opening

explanation: Many small cysts don't hurt or cause any trouble at all. Patients usually only find out about them when a healthcare provider spots them during a routine checkup. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T7#GNS216_U5_T7_h3)

question: Which patient position is standard for examining a vulval cyst?
explanation: The lithotomy position (lying on the back with legs raised in stirrups) gives the best view and access for examining the external female genitalia safely. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T7#GNS216_U5_T7_h4)

question: Why might a doctor order a biopsy for a vulval lump in an older adult patient?

options.A: To measure the exact amount of fluid inside the cyst
options.B: To check and make sure the persistent or unusual mass is not cancerous
options.C: To prove that the cyst started from an infected hair follicle
options.D: To help the fluid sac absorb faster on its own

explanation: Any unusual or stubborn lump in older women needs a quick tissue check (biopsy) just to be 100% sure it isn't malignant. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T7#GNS216_U5_T7_h4)

question: What is the main reason for placing a Word catheter after draining a Bartholin cyst?

options.A: To freeze and destroy the remaining cyst wall cells
options.B: To pump liquid antibiotics directly inside the cavity
options.C: To keep the new drainage opening open so a fresh duct can form
options.D: To permanently stop all fluid production in the body

explanation: The Word catheter has a tiny balloon at the tip and stays in for a few weeks. It keeps the wound open so it can heal into a permanent, normal drainage pathway. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T7#GNS216_U5_T7_h5)

question: How does a procedure called marsupialization stop a Bartholin cyst from coming back?

options.A: By surgically removing the entire gland and surrounding tissue
options.B: By sealing the gland shut so it stops producing any fluid
options.C: By stitching the edges of the cyst open to create a permanent little pouch
options.D: By packing the internal cavity tightly with sterile gauze

explanation: Marsupialization sounds fancy, but it just means sewing the walls of the cyst open so it turns into a tiny pouch. This stops fluid from getting trapped again! [learn more](GNS216_U5_T7#GNS216_U5_T7_h5)

question: What simple self-care step should a nurse teach a patient with a mild vulval cyst?

options.A: Applying ice packs directly to the bare skin for hours
options.B: Wearing tight synthetic underwear to press the swelling down
options.C: Taking warm sitz baths a few times a day
options.D: Scrubbing the area daily with a firm nylon sponge

explanation: Warm sitz baths are wonderful! They ease the tenderness in that sensitive area and can help small cysts drain naturally. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T7#GNS216_U5_T7_h6)

question: Why must nurses strongly advise patients NEVER to squeeze or pop a vulval cyst at home?

options.A: Squeezing can introduce germs and cause a bad infection
options.B: Manual pressure forces the fluid straight into the bloodstream
options.C: It will instantly trigger cancerous cell growth
options.D: Popping it at home permanently removes the gland

explanation: Trying to pop a cyst at home breaks the delicate skin, lets bacteria in, and can easily turn a painless little cyst into a very painful abscess. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T7#GNS216_U5_T7_h6)
